long_biography.plain_text:
IKOS emerged from a partnership between Elena Ambrosiadou and her then husband, mathematician Martin Coward. Coward concentrated on programming, while Ambrosiadou handled the structural, legal, financial and human-resources work. Their complementary roles helped build one of Europe's early systematic hedge-fund businesses.

After Coward left in 2009 amid the breakdown of their marriage and business relationship, Ambrosiadou remained chief executive. She continued directing strategy and serving on IKOS's investment and risk committees. The Cyprus-based firm applies mathematical models and automated execution across currencies, interest rates, commodities, bonds and equity indices, and remains a regulated investment adviser.
